subject: Urgent: Novacare production timeouts, elevated 5xx/429 — retry storm & KV-cache suspect
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@novacare.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: support@novacare.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Production: sudden 504s and timeouts — urgent

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a very sharp uptick in 5xx (504) and 429 errors in our production traffic starting ~13:55 PST. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~9% in ~10 minutes, and customer-facing latency went from ~120ms to multiple seconds before timing out. Our clients started retrying aggressively and we've now got a retry storm — some downstream services are queuing.

Symptoms observed:
- 504s across multiple endpoints (generation, chat streaming) correlated to request queue growth
- 429s when we attempt to throttle at the edge; but the 504s keep propagating
- Spike in p50/p95 token latency and long tail queue depth on your endpoints
- We pushed a model config and batching tweak at ~13:35; suspect that rollout may have triggered it, but not certain.

Attached: grafana screenshot of error spike, sample client logs showing repeated retries. We need an immediate mitigation plan and a timeline for when production will be back to normal. This is impacting enterprise customers — leadership is on standby.

Please escalate.

—Jordan
VP Product, Novacare Health
[Attachment: grafana-500-spike-screenshot.png (PNG, 180KB)]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@novacare.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 504s and timeouts — urgent

Thanks Jordan — sorry you're seeing this. I'm escalating to SRE and CS now. Short immediate asks while we triage:
1) If possible, please pause client-side infinite retry logic for the next 20–30 minutes (set exponential backoff + low retry cap). That will stop the amplifying loop.
2) Share a short window where you can tolerate a rollback/canary (we can revert the 13:35 rollout).
3) We'll need request IDs and a few sample full request/response headers — if you can drop 3 samples into this thread that will help tracing.

We're treating this as a P1. Marcus — can you run the KV-cache hit/miss and batching scheduler checks and propose an immediate mitigation (toggle, config, or quick rollback)? Laura — I'll coordinate the exec briefing once we have a timeline. I'm attaching our incident runbook for the immediate mitigation checklist.

Sooj
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@novacare.ai>, support@novacare.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 504s and timeouts — urgent

Quick triage notes (summary of first 25m):
- Timeline: config push at 13:35 PST changed batching strategy (aggressiveness) and a minor KV-cache allocation tweak. Errors started ~13:55.
- Observed: KV-cache miss rate jumped from ~2% to ~42% for Novacare partitions; concurrent prefix eviction increased sharply. Cache thrash caused per-request cache loads to block worker threads, increasing queueing and timeouts.
- Continuous batching behavior combined with larger per-batch assembly time caused longer head-of-line blocking when cache lookups stalled, magnifying latency. Clients then retried -> increased concurrent inflight -> amplified queue depth -> 504s and 429s.

Immediate mitigations I recommend and can execute in the next 10–25 minutes (low-risk -> higher-risk):
A) Disable continuous batching for Novacare by overriding route config: set batch.max_window_ms=0 for their route. This will reduce queuing and immediate p95 latency. Impact: higher per-token cost but lower tail latency.
B) Force a controlled restart of the serving pool with KV-cache cleared (kubectl rollout restart deployment/novacare-serving) and start with reduced worker concurrency (WORKER_CONCURRENCY=8). This will warm the cache cleanly.
C) Apply a transient edge rate-limit: allow 30rps per client with 5s burst to quickly damp retries, coordinated with Novacare.
D) If rollback requested: revert the 13:35 batching config and redeploy. That is effective but takes ~15–20m to roll out across all nodes.

I'm attaching a KV dump and a trace extract. Next steps: if Soojin/Laura approve, I'll do (A) immediately and (C) with your OK. If Jordan approves rollback we can do (D).

Technical attachment: kv-dump-20261120.tar.gz (contains sample keys and miss-rate traces).
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@novacare.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 504s and timeouts — urgent

Jordan — thanks for the rapid heads-up and for the samples. We own this until it's resolved. Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
- T+0–10m: Marcus to disable continuous batching for Novacare (A) and apply edge rate-limits (C).
- T+10–40m: Validate p95 and error rate drop; if not improved, perform controlled rollback of the 13:35 change (D).
- T+40–120m: Controlled restart with KV-cache flush and warmup if needed (B).
- Executive briefing scheduled: 16:30 PST (we'll call in 20 minutes) — TL;DR, mitigation choices and expected SLA impacts.

If you approve the MAP, please reply "Approve MAP" and we'll begin. As a reminder, we can also offer a one-time operational credit under our SLA if we determine the incident was caused by a Redwood deployment change.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_map_novacare.pdf (PDF, 85KB)]
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@novacare.ai>

Cc: support@novacare.ai

Subject: Re: Production: sudden 504s and timeouts — urgent

Approve MAP. Please execute A and C immediately. If we don't see meaningful improvement in 15 minutes, proceed to rollback (D). I'm on the exec call at 16:30 PST. Please keep me posted in this thread and include any short commands you run so our infra can mirror them if needed.

Also — we'll hold client retry behavior back on our side as requested. Thank you for the rapid response.

—Jordan
VP Product, Novacare Health
